delta: Alex turns toward a fresh blank section of the board, preparing the next topic.
concept: bridge toward the worker-gains chapter

delta: Cut to Maya carrying her individual container physically in her arms as she walks from one office desk shape toward a different one.
concept: visualize portability: Maya physically carries her account across a job change

delta: Maya sets the container down at the new desk; its level is unchanged, clearly hers throughout the move.
concept: personal visibility and control of the account balance

delta: A small simple padlock-and-checkmark icon appears briefly beside the container, indicating direct ownership of the vested balance.
concept: direct ownership of vested account assets

delta: Mr. Carter appears briefly to add a small employer-match arrow into the container at the new job as well.
concept: potential employer matching as a portable-plan advantage

delta: Maya looks at her screen showing the account menu again, comfortably choosing among a few investment options.
concept: employee control within plan choices

delta: A small simple summary row of four icons appears: portability, visibility, control, matching — clean and uncluttered, no crowding.
concept: positive structural changes summarized visually

delta: A small new icon labeled contribution-rate begins to gently hover into the frame near the container, appearing one at a time, not all at once.
concept: new responsibility appears: contribution-rate decisions

delta: A second small icon labeled investment-allocation appears near the first, calmly, without visual clutter.
concept: new responsibility appears: investment-allocation decisions

delta: A third small icon labeled market-volatility appears near the others.
concept: new responsibility appears: exposure to market volatility

delta: A fourth small icon labeled fees appears near the others, the group still calm and orderly, not overwhelming.
concept: new responsibility appears: fees

delta: A fifth and sixth small icon appear together, labeled rollover-decisions and withdrawal-planning.
concept: new responsibilities appear: rollover decisions and retirement withdrawal planning

delta: Camera pulls back to frame Maya calmly beside her container with the six small responsibility icons arranged neatly around it, instructional rather than chaotic.
concept: full responsibility set shown calmly, instructional not overwhelming

delta: Return briefly to split screen: Robert with his steady recurring envelope icons on the left, Maya with her container and responsibility icons on the right.
concept: contrast predictable pension income with flexible, responsibility-laden 401(k) ownership

delta: A caption appears centered beneath the split screen.
concept: state plainly that neither system is simply free money
text_labels: NEITHER SYSTEM IS SIMPLY FREE MONEY.

delta: A second caption line appears beneath the first.
concept: state plainly that responsibility is allocated differently between the systems

delta: Cut to a wide community backdrop showing several distinct simple workplace shapes together for the first time in this chapter. Maya stands near the office-tower shape with her container.
concept: introduce a private worker with a 401(k) as one example among several

delta: Robert stands near a small factory shape with his steady row of envelope icons, positioned elsewhere along the same backdrop.
concept: a private worker with a pension still exists today

delta: A new simple worker icon appears near a government-building shape, connected to both a small pooled-tank icon and a small container icon at once.
concept: some workers have both a pension and a 401(k)-style plan

delta: A new simple worker icon appears clearly beside the government-building shape alone, connected only to a pooled-tank icon of its own.
concept: public-sector workers often participate in separate pension systems

delta: Two more simple worker icons appear: one beside a small shop shape with no plan icon connected at all, and one standing alone labeled self-employed with a small separate retirement-arrangement icon.
concept: some workers have no employer plan; self-employed workers may use other arrangements
text_labels: NO EMPLOYER PLAN   /   SELF-EMPLOYED: OTHER ARRANGEMENT

delta: Camera pulls back to reveal a separate simple foundation layer beneath all the worker icons, labeled distinctly from every plan icon above it.
concept: Social Security exists as a separate federal layer beneath employer plans

delta: Cut to the explanation room one final time. Alex stands centered between Robert on one side and Maya on the other, the board behind them split with the pension structure visible on the left and the 401(k) structure visible on the right.
concept: final scene setup: both structures visible together

camera: medium shot, camera favors the left side
delta: Camera favors the left side of the board, simplifying the pension side down to a short labeled chain: plan manages pooled assets, promises a formula-based benefit, bears substantial funding and investment responsibility.
concept: simplify the pension structure to its essence
text_labels: EMPLOYER/PLAN -> POOLED ASSETS -> FORMULA-BASED BENEFIT -> BEARS FUNDING/INVESTMENT RESPONSIBILITY

camera: medium shot, camera favors the right side
delta: Camera favors the right side of the board, simplifying the 401(k) side down to a short labeled chain: worker and employer contributions, individual account, investments rise and fall, final resources depend on the balance.
concept: simplify the 401(k) structure to its essence
text_labels: WORKER + EMPLOYER CONTRIBUTIONS -> INDIVIDUAL ACCOUNT -> RISES/FALLS -> FINAL RESOURCES = BALANCE

delta: Camera returns to the full wide shot. A single large conceptual weight icon visibly moves from the employer/plan side of the board toward the individual-worker side, though a smaller connected portion visibly remains on the employer side (plan design, administration, contributions, fiduciary duties).
concept: final structural transformation: promised income to individual account, with more risk, more decisions, and more portability moving to the worker, while employer responsibilities do not disappear entirely
text_labels: PROMISED RETIREMENT INCOME -> INDIVIDUAL RETIREMENT ACCOUNT: MORE RISK + MORE DECISIONS + MORE PORTABILITY MOVE TO THE WORKER
